summary: This note describes the nerve as an enclosed, cable-like bundle of axons in the peripheral nervous system, covering its connective tissue layers (epineurium, perineurium, endoneurium), classification into afferent, efferent and mixed nerves, and spinal versus cranial nerves. It also covers nerve function and conduction speed, regeneration after injury, clinical conditions that damage nerves, identified and command neurons in other animals such as the fish Mauthner cells, and historical notes from Herophilos and William Cullen.
one_line: Overview of the nerve as a bundle of axons in the peripheral nervous system, covering its structure, types, function, regeneration, clinical damage and history.
key_facts: A nerve is an enclosed, cable-like bundle of nerve fibers (axons) in the peripheral nervous system.
Each axon is surrounded by a layer of connective tissue called the endoneurium.
Fascicles are wrapped in a layer of connective tissue called the perineurium.
The entire nerve is wrapped in a layer of connective tissue called the epineurium.
Some myelinated neurons conduct action potentials at speeds up to 120 m/s.
Nerves are categorized into afferent, efferent and mixed nerves based on the direction signals are conducted.
All spinal nerves are mixed nerves, and some cranial nerves are also mixed nerves.
Cranial nerves are typically assigned Roman numerals from 1 to 12, although cranial nerve zero is sometimes included.
Nerve regeneration is very slow and can take up to several months to complete.
Multiple sclerosis occurs when the macrophages of an individual's own immune system damage the myelin sheaths that insulate the axon.
Every fish has two Mauthner cells, located in the bottom part of the brainstem, which drive a fast escape response.
Herophilos (335–280 BC) described the functions of the optic nerve in sight and the oculomotor nerve in eye movement.
Modern research has not confirmed William Cullen's 1785 hypothesis associating mental states with physical nerves.
Cancer can spread by invading the spaces around nerves, particularly in head and neck cancer, prostate cancer and colorectal cancer.

entities.name: Mauthner cells
entities.role: gigantic identified neurons of fish, located in the bottom part of the brainstem, that trigger a fast escape response and are described as command neurons

entities.name: Herophilos
entities.role: ancient figure (335–280 BC) who described the functions of the optic and oculomotor nerves and differentiated nerves from blood vessels

entities.name: William Cullen
entities.role: author of an 1785 hypothesis associating mental states with physical nerves, which modern research has not confirmed

entities.name: Schwann cells
entities.role: supportive cells that coat axons in myelin

entities.name: Guillain–Barré syndrome
entities.role: autoimmune disease cited as a cause of nerve damage

entities.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
entities.role: condition causing nerve damage, abbreviated CTS, cited as an example of a pinched nerve

entities.name: Multiple sclerosis
entities.role: disease associated with extensive nerve damage through myelin destruction

entities.name: Notch signaling
entities.role: molecular mechanism that can re-stimulate nerve growth

entities.name: Cnidaria, Ctenophora and Echinodermata
entities.role: organism groups with nerve nets serving as their nervous system
